name: Diffuser curl drying

lead: Diffuser curl drying means drying hair with a wide attachment that spreads the dryer's airflow, so curly, wavy, permed or fine hair keeps defined curls with added volume. Users say it cuts frizz compared with blasting hair with a bare dryer.

Dryer references describe a diffuser as spreading the air so hair dries more slowly, at a lower temperature and with less disturbance, which is said to reduce frizz and add volume. The result is visible once hair is dry and lasts until the next wash. No clinical studies of diffusing were found.

paras: People apply their usual curl products to damp hair, then hold sections of hair in the diffuser bowl or move it around the head on low or medium speed and heat. It is used on wash days in place of air-drying or a bare nozzle. Drying time is longer than with a standard nozzle.
Heat from dryers can leave hair dry and brittle with heavy use, according to hair-care references. No other specific hazards were reported.

angle.text: A diffuser dries curly, wavy or fine hair with softer, spread-out airflow, so curls look more defined, less frizzy and fuller. The look is visible once hair is dry and lasts until the next wash.

lead: Diffuser curl drying is the practice of drying hair with a hair-dryer attachment that spreads the airflow, usually to keep curls and waves defined while adding volume. It is discussed as a styling method for naturally curly, permed and fine hair.[1]
A diffuser is described in dryer references as spreading the airflow so that hair dries more slowly, at a lower temperature and with less disturbance, which is said to reduce frizz and add volume.[1]
No published clinical studies were found on diffusing for curl definition.
infobox: Curly, wavy, permed, fine or colored hair[1]
Less frizz, added volume, curl definition[1]

paras: A hair dryer blows air from a fan over a heating element. Alongside the diffuser, common attachments include a concentrator nozzle that narrows airflow to dry faster and a comb nozzle.[1] Diffusers spread the air over a wider area instead of directing it as a single stream.[1]

Styling with dryers is described as forming temporary hydrogen bonds in the hair, which humidity and washing undo.[1] Proponents of diffusing say the gentler airflow dries curls without scattering them, which they associate with less frizz.
General hair-care references note that hair overheated by dryers and hot irons can become dry and brittle.[2]
